title: ApiGateway — A Secret Worth Guessing
objective: Tokens here are properly signed, with a real signature check — unlike the other ApiGateway. The signing secret just isn't a very good one. Forge an admin token by finding it.

verifier.condition: A request to the admin API succeeds using a JWT the caller forged and signed themselves, with a role claim the server never issued, proving the real signing secret was recovered rather than guessed as a token.

weakness: Tokens are signed correctly with HS256, but the signing secret is a short, common word rather than a long random value, so it can be recovered by trying candidate secrets against a token's own signature offline.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /api/admin/report (Authorization: Bearer <jwt>; signature genuinely verified, but the secret is weak)
seededData: User alice (role user) with a correctly-issued, properly HS256-signed JWT obtainable via login. The signing secret is one short, common word, different each instance, drawn from a small fixed wordlist.

credentials.label: API user
credentials.note: POST /api/login returns a real, correctly-signed token.

hints: This token's signature is real — the alg:none trick from the other lab in this family won't work here. Confirm that for yourself.
An HMAC signature can be recomputed completely offline if you know the secret. You don't need the server's help to test a guess.
The secret is a single short, ordinary word, not a random string — the kind of thing that ends up in a small wordlist.
burpNotes: Get a real token from /api/login, then take its header and payload and recompute the HS256 signature locally for each candidate secret in a short wordlist until one matches the token's actual signature — then build your own forged token with that secret.
